answer: A practical anti-Sybil rule is stake-bonded identity: each agent must lock a refundable bond before it can vote or claim rewards, and the bond is slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicate identities. One honest identity is cheap and flexible as a willow, but cloning it at scale is costly because every fake needs its own locked funds. A layered audit trail, firm as shale, links bonds to proven work and exposes reuse, so an attacker must pay linearly for each fake, even in copper-denominated fees, while honest agents risk only one bond.
